shared: The Viper, known to Inner Sphere forces by its reporting name Dragonfly, is a 40-ton Clan OmniMech first produced in 2940 by Clan Fire Mandrill on the world of Shadow. Conceived as a quick-strike design emphasizing speed and agility over raw firepower, the Viper initially fell out of favor with several Fire Mandrill kindraa due to persistent problems with its omnipod mechanisms. In 3002, the Mandrills traded the design specifications and manufacturing facilities to Clan Ghost Bear in exchange for several production runs of Executioner OmniMechs. The Ghost Bears relocated production to Strana Mechty, developing modular production line technology in the process that would later prove invaluable during their migration to the Inner Sphere. Despite its troubled origins, the Viper has endured as one of the most widely distributed medium OmniMechs in the Clan arsenal, with production eventually spreading to multiple facilities across both the Homeworlds and the Inner Sphere.

Built on a lightweight Type W2 Endo-steel chassis and powered by a 320-rated XL engine, the Viper achieves a top speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, making it one of the fastest medium OmniMechs in any Clan touman. Eight jump jets provide an impressive 240-meter jump capability, granting exceptional tactical flexibility in broken or urban terrain. Seven tons of ferro-fibrous armor provide reasonable protection for its weight class, though the design remains vulnerable to concentrated fire from heavier opponents.

The Viper's primary limitation is its modest 8.5 tons of pod space, which significantly restricts its offensive payload compared to other medium OmniMechs in the 35-to-45-ton range such as the Adder, Shadow Cat, and Grendel. In its Prime configuration, the Viper mounts a pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher for close-range engagements, supported by twin machine guns for anti-infantry work and an anti-missile system for defensive purposes. While considered undergunned for formal Clan dueling, the Viper excels in the fluid, indirect combat typical of Inner Sphere operations, where its speed allows it to choose engagements and screen for heavier formations.

The Viper's early history is defined by a pattern of ownership changes that would shape its manufacturing legacy for centuries. Originally produced by Kindraa Sainze of Clan Fire Mandrill on Shadow, the design's troubled relationship with the Fire Mandrills' fractious internal politics led to its transfer to Clan Ghost Bear in 3002. Rather than Trial for land rights on Shadow and become embroiled in inter-Kindraa conflicts, the Ghost Bears restructured the production facility into a modular design and physically relocated the entire manufacturing line to their enclave on Strana Mechty. This innovative modular approach to production would prove to be one of the Viper's most significant, if unintended, legacies. When the Ghost Bears began their migration back to the Inner Sphere in the late 3050s, the modular factory technology developed for the Viper line allowed them to move several other manufacturing operations with relative ease.

Production on Strana Mechty continued under Ghost Bear control until the mid-3060s, when Clan Hell's Horses trialed for and won both production rights and the Upsilon Plant 2J facility. Their tenure was short-lived, however, as Clan Ice Hellion seized the entire plant in early 3068 following a grueling twelve-hour battle between both saKhans. The Ice Hellions immediately put the facility to use, with new configurations being shipped out as quickly as DropShips could be loaded, lending credence to rumors of a planned large-scale operation against their Coyote neighbors on Foster.

Beyond Strana Mechty, additional Viper production existed across the Homeworlds. Clan Coyote maintained a manufacturing line on Delios until 3071, when Clan Goliath Scorpion captured the facility during the opening stages of the Wars of Reaving. The Cloud Cobras operated their own production lines on Homer and at the Albion Armor Works on Albion. Clan Blood Spirit also maintained early production capacity at the Albion facility before the Star Adders assumed control. Following the Wars of Reaving and the destruction or Abjuration of several Clans, the surviving Home Clans continued to field the Viper as the similar Ice Ferret was phased out, possibly due to its association with the departed Spheroid Clans.

Having abandoned their Homeworld production infrastructure, the Ghost Bears, now reorganized as the Rasalhague Dominion, ultimately resumed Viper production at the newly established Dominion Facility Kappa-5 on Thule. This ensured the design remained a fixture within the Dominion's touman well into the Dark Age, where continued deployment in the Inner Sphere demonstrated that the Viper's combination of speed, mobility, and reconfiguration flexibility remained as tactically relevant as ever.

The Vulcan carries an unusual weapons array optimized for anti-personnel operations rather than 'Mech-to-'Mech combat. Its primary armaments are a Firestorm flamer and Sperry Browning machine gun, both devastating against unarmored troops and capable of clearing buildings with brutal efficiency. The Armstrong Autocannon/2, while originally intended to provide anti-'Mech capability, proved more effective as an anti-building weapon given its limited stopping power against armored targets. A Randell medium laser serves as backup when the autocannon's ammunition runs dry.

The Vulcan's true strength lies in its exceptional mobility for urban operations. Six rear-mounted jump jets, specially vented to reduce heat buildup, provide 180 meters of jumping capability, allowing pilots to rapidly reposition across rooftops and obstacles. A top speed of 97 kilometers per hour complements this agility, making the Vulcan difficult to pin down in close terrain.

However, the design carries significant limitations. With only five tons of armor, the Vulcan cannot sustain prolonged engagements against heavier opponents and is rarely deployed without support from larger BattleMechs. The absence of manipulative hands further restricts close combat options, though this limitation proves minor given the 'Mech's intended role of infantry suppression rather than dueling.

shared:
The Warhammer was introduced in 2515 by StarCorps Industries as a heavy fire-support platform capable of anchoring battle lines and devastating opponents at range. Designed in response to a procurement request for a mobile 'Mech with enough firepower to destroy or severely damage any 'Mech of the same weight class or lower, StarCorps delivered what would become one of the most iconic BattleMechs in history. The seventy-ton chassis quickly proved itself across every major conflict of the Star League era, earning a reputation as the backbone of heavy and battle regiments and a favorite mount of the legendary Star League Gunslingers.

Produced under license by manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery, the Warhammer's proliferation is rivaled by few designs. Its combination of devastating long-range firepower, respectable protection, and adaptable chassis has ensured a steady supply across all eras of warfare, with demand only increasing with each new conflict. Few BattleMech designs can claim as broad and continuous a production history as the Warhammer.

The Warhammer almost defines the heavy weight class of BattleMechs. Its rugged, stable chassis carries a pair of deadly arm-mounted particle projection cannons that give the design dependable firepower at range, capable of threatening even the heaviest armor. A six-tube Holly short-range missile system supplements these primary weapons and is itself backed by pairs of medium and small lasers and SperryBrowning machine guns, providing a layered defensive suite against infantry and light 'Mechs that close to exploit the PPC minimum range. This combination ensures the Warhammer remains dangerous at every engagement bracket.

With a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, the Warhammer can keep pace with most battle formations and its eighteen heat sinks allow it the freedom to move and fire without undue concern over heat buildup during sustained engagements. Respectable armor protection enables the design to absorb significant punishment while maintaining combat effectiveness, though the lack of jump capability limits its tactical flexibility in broken terrain. Dated but competitive electronics, including the O/P 3000 COMSET communications suite and O/P 1500 ARB targeting and tracking system, make the Warhammer equally capable of serving in the line of combat or in a command slot, a versatility that has kept it at the forefront of heavy lance doctrine for over five centuries.

The Warhammer may be the best representation of the average citizen's view of the BattleMech. From the unwavering lines of the Star League Defense Force bringing down the Usurper, to the Periphery pirate screaming "Stand and Deliver," the Warhammer looms large over popular images of BattleMech warfare. First deployed in 2515, the design has served admirably in every major action in the Inner Sphere and beyond, from the liberation of Terra from Stefan Amaris to the bloody fields of Marduk in 3039. Every Successor State military makes use of the design, and it is held in high regard by mercenaries and Periphery nations alike.

Perhaps the most famous chapter in the Warhammer's long battlefield history occurred during the Marik Civil War in 3015, when Wolf's Dragoons fought their way through Duke Anton Marik's forces in engagements that became the stuff of legend. The fighting on Anton's New Delos saw Warhammers on both sides pushing their heat sinks to the limit in brutal close-quarters engagements that demonstrated the design's durability under extreme conditions. The Spirit Cat allies later witnessed the effectiveness of Marik Warhammers firsthand when the Regulan Hussars invaded Marik in 3147, where fire lances built around the design provided devastating covering fire for faster striker elements.

The Federated Commonwealth's Warhammer production capacity suffered a significant blow with the loss of the 'Mech's primary Olivetti factory on Sudeten to Clan Jade Falcon early in the Clan Invasion. The Commonwealth was reduced to refitting ancient Succession Wars machines to the -7S standard until Project Phoenix brought new Warhammers to the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth more than a decade later. Clan garrisons also developed various ClanTech refit kits for use on captured FedCom Warhammers, replacing the PPCs with pulse lasers on models not yet equipped with double heat sinks. The recovery of the Helm Core brought about a new generation of Warhammer variants, first in the form of refit kits and later with new production variants employing reclaimed technology, with extended-range cannons and improved heat-dissipating technology making an effective combination even against the Clan invaders.

The Free Worlds League found a booming business in the export of Warhammer refit kits in the years before and after the Clan Invasion, and the popularity of their kits and the deals made with other Houses during the conflict made Free Worlds League Warhammers ubiquitous throughout the Inner Sphere. Production of new units within the League was limited until early in the Jihad, when the Prince of Regulus backed a new Warhammer line on Wallis to supply BattleMechs for his ambitious plans. The Draconis Combine refit its own Warhammers to the -7K standard, and when a variant featuring paired heavy PPCs proved popular enough that other Houses began copying it, Alshain Weapons received funding to build a new Warhammer production line on Tok Do. With the renewed emphasis on tradition in the Draconis Combine, Alshain emphasized the classic chassis on all their Warhammers.

Wolf's Dragoons contracted to begin production runs on a Golden Century-era Clan Warhammer variant which was popular with the original Dragoons, fulfilling several Clans' subsequent requests for the model. The Taurian Concordat has constructed the Warhammer on Pinard since the 'Mech was first introduced, and after the discovery of the New Dallas Memory Core during the Jihad, SLDF Royal models were introduced into production. After the asteroid attack on Taurus, TTI CEO Matthias Commager won reconstruction bids that not only funded facility refurbishment but brought attention to a revitalized Taurus Territorial Industries, which chose the Warhammer as its new flagship product.

shared: The Warhawk, designated Masakari by Inner Sphere forces after a Japanese battle-axe of medieval Terra, is an 85-ton Clan assault OmniMech introduced by Clan Smoke Jaguar in 2999. Developed at the Phan Industriplex on Huntress, the design was conceived as part of the Jaguars' military buildup in anticipation of the long-awaited return to the Inner Sphere. When the Dragoon Compromise temporarily shelved invasion plans, the Smoke Jaguars instead turned the Warhawk against their Warden rivals, demonstrating its devastating firepower in inter-Clan conflicts. The design achieved its greatest notoriety during the Clan Invasion, where it became a symbol of Jaguar frontline power and was frequently deployed alongside the Dire Wolf in devastating assault formations. Production remained a jealously guarded Jaguar monopoly until the Clan's annihilation, after which manufacturing knowledge spread to the Fire Mandrills, Diamond Sharks, and Goliath Scorpions.

The Warhawk is built around a General Systems 340 XL engine providing a top speed of 64 km/h, adequate for an assault platform but unremarkable for its weight class. The chassis mounts thirteen and a half tons of Forging X85 ferro-fibrous armor, providing substantial protection while freeing weight for the design's impressive thirty-two and a half tons of pod space. Twenty fixed double heat sinks represent an over-engineered cooling system that enables the Warhawk to mount energy-heavy configurations without crippling heat buildup. The design lacks jump jets entirely, committing fully to the direct-fire assault role.

A distinctive feature of the Warhawk is the incorporation of an advanced Targeting Computer into virtually every configuration, granting exceptional accuracy to its direct-fire weapons. This combination of targeting precision and generous pod space makes the ER PPC the signature weapon across many loadouts. Space constraints imposed by the targeting computer and cooling infrastructure mean that large-bore autocannons are infrequently mounted, as the complex routing of ammunition feeds proves impractical within the remaining volume. Where the Warhawk excels is in delivering accurate direct-energy barrages that leave enemy 'Mechs crippled but salvageable, a quality prized by Clan warriors who value the spoils of combat.

The Warhawk's history is inextricably linked to Clan Smoke Jaguar. Created in 2999 as the Jaguars prepared for the anticipated return to the Inner Sphere, the design was one of the most powerful OmniMechs of its era. The Dragoon Compromise of 3000 delayed those plans, and the Jaguars instead deployed their new weapon against Warden Clans to devastating effect. All examples of the Warhawk outside Jaguar toumans during this period were exclusively battlefield salvage, as the Jaguars maintained absolute control over the Phan Industriplex production line on Huntress.

The Warhawk truly came into its own during the Clan Invasion of 3049, where DCMS warriors of the Draconis Combine bestowed the codename Masakari upon the fearsome assault 'Mech. Deployed extensively along the Jaguar Invasion Corridor and frequently paired with the Dire Wolf, the Warhawk became the iconic symbol of Smoke Jaguar military dominance. Though other Clans such as the Ghost Bears and Jade Falcons fielded captured examples, the Jaguars' production monopoly held firm throughout the Invasion era.

The annihilation of Clan Smoke Jaguar during Operation Serpent and the Great Refusal fundamentally altered the Warhawk's production environment. Inner Sphere forces made a cursory effort to raze the Phan Industriplex during the assault on Huntress, but enough of the complex survived that Clan Fire Mandrill's Kindraa Kline, which had maintained a separate production facility on Dagda, seized control and rebuilt one Warhawk production line. The Fire Mandrills subsequently traded the design to the Diamond Sharks, who established their own production at Manufacturing Plant DSF-94 on Vinton. The Goliath Scorpions also acquired production capability during this period.

The Jihad severed contact between the Inner Sphere Clans and the Homeworlds, cutting off any possibility of resupply. Warhawks among the Jade Falcons, Ghost Bears, and Wolves-in-Exile became increasingly rare, their numbers reduced by attrition as patchwork repairs and mismatched components became the norm for surviving examples. By the ilClan era, the once-powerful symbol of Smoke Jaguar dominance had become a rarity in the Inner Sphere.

In the Deep Periphery, the Goliath Scorpions took extraordinary measures to preserve their Warhawks following their Abjurement, cannibalizing severely damaged chassis to keep others operational. Cherishing the design for its pinpoint accuracy, the Scorpions revived production prior to the Hanseatic Crusade, where the Warhawk played a key role in the Escorpión Imperio's conquest of the Hanseatic League. The wealth of resources captured during the Crusade allowed the new Scorpion Empire to retool the factory on Antwerp at Imperial BattleMechs, fully resurrecting the Warhawk production line. Clan Sea Fox has expressed interest in purchasing the design, but the Scorpions have thus far refused all outside sales, prioritizing their own internal needs.

shared: The Watchman is a forty-ton BattleMech born from the political and military pressures of the Clan Invasion era. When First Prince Hanse Davion stripped frontline units from the Draconis March to face the advancing Clans, Duke Aaron Sandoval demanded recompense for leaving his border vulnerable. The compromise was a new militia 'Mech based on the proven Enforcer chassis, designed for rapid and inexpensive production at Robinson Standard BattleWorks. Entering service in 3055, the Watchman was built with readily available off-the-shelf components to ensure ease of repair and maintenance by militia technicians, establishing itself as a durable and reliable garrison design suited to training and border defense roles throughout the Federated Suns.

The Watchman shares the Dorwinion Standard chassis and Nissan 200 engine of the original Enforcer, giving the lighter forty-ton design a brisk top speed of 86 km/h. Five HildCo Model 12 jump jets provide a 150-meter jump capability, making the Watchman surprisingly agile for a garrison design. Eight and a half tons of Starshield A armor with CASE provide respectable protection, while the simplified cockpit layout was specifically designed to accommodate less experienced MechWarriors, making the Watchman an excellent training platform.

The Watchman's armament trades the Enforcer's autocannon for a more maintenance-friendly weapons suite. A ChisComp 43 Special large laser serves as the primary weapon, providing good medium-to-long range striking power without the ammunition dependency of ballistic weapons. Two ChisComp 39 medium lasers handle close-range defense, while a pair of Sperry Browning machine guns deter infantry attacks. This all-energy primary armament with minimal ammunition requirements reflects the design's garrison role, where sustained operation without reliable supply lines is a constant concern. The trade-off is a lack of concentrated striking power compared to heavier designs, requiring Watchman pilots to rely on mobility and coordinated fire to engage serious threats.

The Watchman's creation was driven by the intersection of Clan Invasion-era strategic realities and Draconis March politics. When the bulk of the AFFS redeployed to face the Clans, Duke Aaron Sandoval of Robinson leveraged his political influence to secure funding for a new militia 'Mech. Hanse Davion agreed to share financing for the project, and Robinson Standard BattleWorks (previously a minor equipment supplier) was expanded and upgraded to full BattleMech manufacture. The Watchman was designed to maximize parts commonality with the existing Enforcer, using the same chassis, engine, and similar armor to minimize production costs and ensure ready access to spare parts.

The Watchman proved itself during the fighting on Proserpina between 3062 and 3063, where Robinson Battle Academy cadets and militia formations equipped with the design demonstrated its effectiveness in real combat. Demand for the Watchman increased significantly during the FedCom Civil War, as border militias found themselves bearing increased responsibility for regional defense. Duke Sandoval used allocation of Watchman production as a political tool, distributing the 'Mechs to reward political allies and consolidate his influence within the Draconis March.

The Watchman's legacy extends beyond its own production run, serving as the foundation for the Sentry and Cuirass designs that followed. Robinson Standard BattleWorks built on the success of the Watchman to establish itself as a significant manufacturer within the Federated Suns, eventually producing far more advanced designs including the Atlas III. The WTC-4DM upgrade, developed after James Sandoval's incursion into the Draconis Combine, brought the Watchman closer to frontline capability with a PPC, double heat sinks, and ferro-fibrous armor, reflecting the evolving demands placed on what was originally conceived as a simple garrison design.

The Jihad and its aftermath saw Robinson Standard BattleWorks struggle under contested ownership, with the factory falling under provisional Federated Suns control during the conflict before stabilizing in the early Republic era. Watchman production had already ceased by that point, but the design remained in widespread militia service across the Draconis March. The Draconis Combine's invasion of the region in the mid-thirty-second century thrust the aging Watchman back into the spotlight, as garrison units equipped with the venerable design found themselves facing modern Combine forces employing advanced armor composites. Militia technicians responded with the WTC-4DM2 field refit, stripping the original weapons suite entirely and replacing it with a large re-engineered laser and supporting arms specifically chosen to defeat the Combine's specialty plating. The Watchman also found an unexpected second life on the Solaris VII dueling circuit, where its rugged chassis and easy maintenance proved attractive to smaller stables seeking a reliable platform for aftermarket modification.

shared.overview: Even in the oldest Terran legends, the raven is an opportunist and scavenger, unashamed of feasting on a rotting carcass. In the case of the White Raven, the carcass was that of Clan Steel Viper, and their Black Python. The Ravens always lamented seeing the graceful, bird-like Black Python in Viper formations, feeling that such a ’Mech should be soaring with them rather than slithering with the hated Vipers. By resurrecting the pre-3060s Black Python under a new name, Clan Snow Raven is merely staying true to form. The new ’Mech has been successful enough to erase the memory of its old Spheroid name. There is no more Viper, only the White Raven.
shared.capabilities: Lacking the knockout punch of a large-bore autocannon or Gauss rifle, the Black Python whittled down its enemies with pulse laser fire. While this decreased accidental deaths during duels, prolonged combat saw the ’Mech disabled more often than not, leading to its pilots being shunted into the ignominious role of hunting lighter units. The new White Raven is an exemplary sniper, meant to harass at range with precise fire. The decision to wrap the chassis in ferro-lamellor armor seems to have been a test bed for newer Raven OmniMechs like the War Crow, which shares many design features with the White Raven.
shared.battleHistory: The Ravens were deeply disturbed when recent clashes with the Federated Suns revealed the Davions using a weapon that ignored the Clan’s precious ferro-lamellor armor. Though re-engineered lasers had been deployed for several years, the Ravens had discounted them as an inferior Spheroid development. Khan McKenna wanted to acquire some of these weapons for study, but after Palmyra the Suns was open to neither Raven merchants nor friendly Trials. Instead, Khan McKenna assembled a special R-team under Lucien Clearwater, the Red Raven, to acquire a sample or die trying.:br::br::tab:The Raven Watch turned up a possible target on Winfield with the Second Periphery Guards: AFFS Major Jonathan Baines, and his VTR-12D Victor. Clearwater relished the challenge of drawing out a high-ranking officer in a dangerous BattleMech, and his team inserted itself onto Winfield. It took nearly two months of hit-and-fade raids before this unClanlike behavior finally drew out Major Baines, who personally took the field with a lance to put an end to what he thought was pirate activity. The confrontation inside Bryce Canyon claimed all of Clearwater’s infantry, who held back the Guards while Lucien dueled with Baines. Only the White Raven’s ferro-lamellor saved Lucien from the Victor’s Gauss rifle as he focused long-range precision fire on the Davion ’Mech’s left arm, finally blowing it off just as the Victor breached his armor and destroying the Raven’s targeting computer. Lucien’s remaining comrade rushed in and retrieved the arm, and both managed to disengage and return to the Alliance with their new prize.
shared.variants: Black Python variants focused on increasing direct-fire capabilities, usually with ER lasers and autocannons. An older Steel Viper refit addressed the lack of a knockout weapon with PPCs and a Gauss rifle. The latest model uses improved jump jets for maximum mobility; only the most skilled warriors are awarded the right to pilot this astonishingly expensive White Raven.
shared.notableUnits: Star Commander Lucien Clearwater: Known as the Red Raven for his tendency to end every trial covered in blood, Lucien has twice achieved the rank of Star Captain, only to lose it again through recklessness. In his decade as a warrior, he has made many grave enemies, lost seven ’Mechs, three fingers, and his right eye, all without ever seeing heavy combat, and all without ever losing his flippant attitude and dashing charm. Rather than dump him in a dezgra unit, Khan McKenna has reassigned Lucien to the Raven Watch. His latest mission, working with the Brotherhood of Randis on a strike against Tortuga, has helped strengthen ties with Randis, as well as proven the value of the White Raven.:br::br:MechWarrior Andrew (Cluetain): Andrew Cluetain initially tried out as an AMC aerospace pilot, but could not keep pace in the competitive selection process. Accepted to Raven MechWarrior training as a freeborn warrior, where it was expected he would flush out early, Andrew channeled his burning anger into victory and attained his MechWarrior rank in record time. Initially assigned to an aging and broken-down Timber Wolf, Andrew defeated two Trueborn warriors in hand-to-hand combat for the right to pilot a new White Raven. The Raven’s sleek, almost LAM-like curves let him dream that he is soaring the skies of Lushann. Though he would make a fine recruit for the Alliance Air Wings, Andrew scoffs at a career of pirate hunting and garrison duty. At least in his White Raven, he is a true warrior.

text.deployment: Designed to engage at multiple ranges, the Alternate Configuration D carries an LRM-5 for long-range harassment, two ER medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 for medium-to-close engagement, and an ER small laser for point-blank defense. This mixed-range loadout provides greater tactical flexibility than most Viper configurations, allowing MechWarriors to adapt to changing battlefield conditions without sacrificing effectiveness at any particular range bracket.

Introduced during the Civil War era, the Alternate Configuration E replaces the separate missile systems found on the D configuration with a single ATM-6 launcher capable of filling multiple range brackets through its variable munitions. An ER medium laser and two ER small lasers round out the direct-fire capability, giving this configuration excellent adaptability for reconnaissance-in-force missions where engagement ranges cannot be predicted in advance.

A Clan Ghost Bear development, the Alternate Configuration G centers on a plasma cannon as its primary weapon, providing both thermal disruption and direct damage capability against enemy units. A heavy medium laser supplements the main armament, while four anti-personnel Gauss rifles offer a high-velocity deterrent against unarmored targets. This versatile mix makes the G configuration effective across a range of close-combat scenarios.

Built around the heavy laser concept that emerged during the Civil War era, the Alternate Configuration H combines two ER medium lasers with two heavy medium lasers and two small pulse lasers, creating a configuration with concentrated short-to-medium range firepower. An anti-missile system provides additional survivability, compensating somewhat for the design's need to close with opponents to bring its full arsenal to bear.

Produced by Clan Ice Hellion after seizing the Upsilon Plant 2J facility on Strana Mechty in 3068, the Alternate Configuration I combines three heavy medium lasers linked to a targeting computer with an ATM-3 launcher for flexible missile support. A light active probe enhances battlefield awareness while an anti-missile system provides defensive coverage, creating a well-integrated reconnaissance and strike configuration that emphasizes precision fire.

Introduced in the Recognition Guide era, the Alternate Configuration J mounts three ATM-3 launchers in the left arm with three tons of ammunition, providing flexible engagement options through variable munitions. ER micro lasers in the right arm and right torso offer lightweight backup firepower, with the expectation that the ATM launchers will serve as the configuration's primary offensive system across all range brackets.

Configured as an advanced electronic warfare scout, the Alternate Configuration K combines two ER medium lasers with three AP Gauss rifles and a ton of ammunition for anti-infantry work. The true strength of this configuration lies in its electronics suite: a TAG designator for calling in artillery and missile strikes, an active probe for detecting hidden units, and an Angel ECM suite for disrupting enemy sensors and communications. This makes the K configuration an ideal forward observer and intelligence-gathering platform.

A fast sniper variant, the Alternate Configuration L carries three Streak LRM-5 launchers distributed across both arms and the left torso, providing accurate long-range fire without the waste of missed volleys. Two ER micro lasers in the right torso offer minimal close-range backup, with the expectation that pilots will exploit the Viper's exceptional speed to maintain standoff distance and avoid close engagements entirely.

Designed for maximum close-range accuracy, the Alternate Configuration M mounts an ER medium laser and medium pulse laser in each arm alongside a micro pulse laser in the right torso, with all weapons linked to an advanced targeting computer. This configuration maximizes hit probability during close engagements, making it one of the most accurate Viper loadouts available and particularly effective against fast-moving targets that other configurations might struggle to track.

The primary configuration balances close-range striking power with defensive capability. A pair of medium pulse lasers and an SRM-4 launcher provide the main offensive punch, while twin machine guns offer anti-infantry suppression and an anti-missile system helps mitigate incoming missile fire. This well-rounded loadout makes this variant configuration a versatile scout and screening platform capable of handling a variety of short-range engagements.

A mixed-technology configuration reflecting the cross-pollination of Clan and Inner Sphere equipment that followed Operation BULLDOG, the Alternate Configuration R combines Clan ER medium lasers with an Inner Sphere-manufactured Bloodhound active probe and a light TAG designator. A NARC missile beacon launcher with two tons of pods rounds out the electronics-heavy loadout, creating a dedicated target acquisition platform that enhances the effectiveness of an entire Star's missile-equipped units.

A Tiburon Khanate refresh of the classic Prime concept, the Alternate Configuration T pairs two ER medium lasers with a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy and adds two ER micro lasers for close defense. A Streak SRM-4 launcher with ammunition provides reliable short-range punch, while a light active probe and anti-missile system enhance survivability and battlefield awareness, representing a modernized take on the Viper's traditional screening role.

Designed for hostile environment operations including boarding actions and space combat, the Alternate Configuration U carries liquid storage tanks for additional reaction mass alongside an ECM suite for electronic concealment during approach. Two ER medium lasers provide ranged firepower, while a hatchet in the left arm allows the pilot to breach enemy hull armor in close quarters. This unusual but effective tool makes the U configuration one of the few Viper loadouts specifically designed for zero-gravity boarding operations.

A Society configuration developed during the Wars of Reaving, the Alternate Configuration Z mounts a Nova CEWS to compensate for the generally lower skill levels of Society MechWarriors. A pair of improved heavy medium lasers in the right arm and a single improved heavy medium laser with an iATM-3 in the left arm provide the offensive punch, while a light TAG designator enables artillery coordination and a laser anti-missile system provides efficient point defense without ammunition dependency.

text.overview:
The Vulcan was designed in 2775 as a dedicated anti-infantry BattleMech during the final years of the Amaris Civil War. As Star League Defense Force troops fought Republican soldiers in the urban centers of the Terran Hegemony, conventional 'Mechs proved vulnerable to dug-in infantry formations. MatherTechno Incorporated of Northwind answered this tactical need by creating a 'Mech specifically equipped to eliminate infantry concentrations while maintaining exceptional mobility in confined city streets.

General Aleksandr Kerensky personally ordered MatherTechno's newly liberated production lines converted to manufacture the Vulcan, recognizing the urgent need for such a specialized platform. The design's distinctive narrow profile earned it the nickname "Scarecrow" among MechWarriors, a reflection of its ungainly but effective silhouette. Production continued at Northwind until the factory's destruction early in the First Succession War, after which the Lyran Commonwealth and Free Worlds League maintained limited manufacturing through Coventry Metal Works and Nimakachi Fusion Products respectively.
text.deployment: This field modification was employed during the failed Davion assault on Vega in the War of 3039. The pilot removed the machine guns, their ammunition, and the medium laser to mount two additional flamers and a small laser, creating a configuration optimized for maximum incendiary effect against infantry and structures. While the modification sacrificed anti-armor capability entirely, it proved devastatingly effective in its intended urban clearance role. The variant represents the type of field expedient commonly seen during extended campaigns where spare parts and tactical requirements drive creative solutions.
text.battleHistory:
The Vulcan's combat debut came during Operation Liberation, the SLDF's final campaign to free Terra from Stefan Amaris in 2779. Serving with the Volunteer Regiments, the design quickly established its reputation as a fearsome urban fighter, its flamers and machine guns proving devastatingly effective against Republican holdouts in Terra's cities. By the Star League's dissolution, every Great House had acquired a sizable inventory of Vulcans.

The First Succession War brought catastrophe when MatherTechno's Northwind facility was destroyed within months of the conflict's outbreak. The Lyran Commonwealth and Free Worlds League salvaged the design specifications, awarding production rights to Coventry Metal Works and Nimakachi Fusion Products Limited respectively. Other Houses maintained their Vulcans through salvage and careful husbandry of remaining spare parts. The Federated Suns especially employed their Vulcans during the reconquest of Kentares IV, where the 'Mechs' flamers devastated Kuritan infantry positions in the cities of Amishton and Davisbury. House Kurita's own Vulcan contingent achieved notoriety during a 3020 raid on Dobson that decimated key Davion aerospace fighter installations.

House Liao suffered the greatest losses, having concentrated most of their Vulcans on Sappho when that world fell to House Marik during the Second Succession War. The Capellan Confederation consequently fielded the fewest Vulcans of any Great House throughout the remaining Succession Wars era.

The recovery of Star League technology enabled Nimakachi to introduce the upgraded VT-5M in 3052, scaling production to twenty units monthly before the Word of Blake's destruction of their Tematagi plant in 3069. Coventry Metal Works developed their own modernized variant, the VT-5S, which saw extensive service during the FedCom Civil War as part of Victor Steiner-Davion's Allied forces. The Word of Blake acquired numerous Vulcans both through purchase and seizure, finding the design invaluable for policing Protectorate cities during the Jihad.

By the thirty-second century, collapsing sales prompted an unprecedented collaboration between Coventry and Nimakachi, resulting in the VT-7T variant that combined the strengths of both manufacturing traditions. This joint venture restored the Vulcan's market position, reaffirming its status as the premier urban combat 'Mech.

text.deployment: This heavily modified VT-5M debuted in 3143 at The Scrapyard arena on Solaris VII, operated by Team Genie. Aftermarket modifications include a retractable blade, Stealth Armor, Angel ECM Suite, and paired Thunderbolt-5 launchers replacing the original weapons loadout. The combination of stealth systems and built-up terrain allows the 'Mech to conceal itself before striking with surprise attacks, a tactic well-suited to tag team matches and exhibition games. The Aladdin rarely appears outside controlled arena environments like the Fantasy Tournament, its specialized configuration proving too limited for conventional military operations.

text.overview:
The Vulpes was introduced in 3133 by Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon, entering service with the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns barely a year after the HPG Blackout plunged the Inner Sphere into chaos. Designed as a heavy, fast attack BattleMech in the same vein as the venerable Argus, the sixty-ton Vulpes was built from the outset to mix Clan-grade technology with advanced Inner Sphere systems, a combination that gave it capabilities few contemporaries could match.

The Vulpes was conceived to fight at extended range, using its advanced defensive systems to shield it from return fire while it closed to effective engagement distance. Fast enough to keep pace with the battle line and dangerous enough that enemies learned quickly not to ignore it, the design's combination of speed, protection, and firepower found an immediate home in the regiments of House Davion.
text.capabilities:
The Vulpes is the AFFS' preeminent heavy attack BattleMech, designed to engage at range and exploit its advanced defensive systems. Its primary armament consists of two ExoStar Pinnacle Clan-specification extended range large lasers mounted in the arms, providing devastating long-range firepower that can outreach most Inner Sphere opponents. Complementing these is a Mydron Tornado rotary class 5 autocannon in the right torso, fed by two tons of ammunition stored in the left torso and protected by CASE. This weapons suite allows the Vulpes to engage effectively at long range while maintaining sustained firepower as engagements close.

The Model 42b 300 XXL engine pushes the Vulpes to a cruising speed of 54 kilometers per hour, with a maximum of 86 that can be boosted to 108 with MASC. Twelve and a half tons of StarGuard Nightshroud stealth armor, working in concert with the integrated Guardian ECM Suite, makes the Vulpes remarkably difficult to target at range. This defensive suite defines the design philosophy, as the Vulpes is intended to fight where its stealth systems provide maximum advantage rather than brawling at close quarters.

The reliance on an XXL engine and stealth armor does create vulnerabilities. The engine is notoriously fragile under concentrated torso fire, and the stealth system's complexity has earned the Vulpes a reputation as difficult to maintain. These trade-offs are considered acceptable given the tactical advantages the design provides when properly employed.
text.deployment:
The VLP-1DX, known as "The Beast," is a radical custom modification that debuted at the New Hartford Gardens Arena on Solaris VII in 3144. Built as a remote-operated drone controlled from the copilot seat of an accompanying Watchman BattleMech designated "Belle," the Beast was personally modified by its operator for Team Teapot, with funding from a grant provided by the Duchy of Andurien. The conversion strips the standard Vulpes philosophy entirely, replacing the XXL engine with a smaller Clan 240 XL that sacrifices roughly a third of the original's speed in exchange for improved durability. The stealth armor system is discarded in favor of Anti-Penetrative Ablation Armor, and an experimental RISC Advanced Point Defense System, developed somewhere inside the Republic after the HPG Blackout, provides additional missile defense.

The Beast's most distinctive features are its claws and talons, which are fully functional melee weapons capable of gouging through layers of battlefield armor in a single strike. Paired with a Clan extended range large laser, a Clan extended range medium pulse laser, and twin ER flamers, the Beast operates as a dedicated close-combat brawler with minimal ranged capability. The weight devoted to its physical weapon protrusions leaves little room for conventional armament, making the Beast a specialized arena fighter rather than a practical battlefield design.
text.battleHistory:
The Vulpes emerged during one of the most turbulent periods in Inner Sphere history, entering production in 3133 as the Blackout signaled the end of Devlin Stone's vision for a peaceful Republic. Achernar BattleMechs responded to the crisis faster than most manufacturers, recognizing the AFFS' urgent need for a modern heavy attack platform. The design found immediate acceptance among Davion commanders, who deployed it to their most elite formations as quickly as production lines could deliver.

Vulpes BattleMechs earned a fearsome reputation in the short time they served in the field. Popular among the AFFS' most elite regiments, they fought in some of the heaviest actions of the period's numerous border conflicts and invasions. On Almach, a pair of Vulpes attached to the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry led two lances of Red Lancers on an extended pursuit, demonstrating the design's combination of speed and endurance. When heavy Arrow IV bombardments forced several detachments to hunt for the launchers, the two MechWarriors instead stumbled upon reconnaissance lances probing the Armored Cavalry's flank. Activating their stealth systems, they engaged from long range, trusting their Clan-specification large lasers to outrange anything the Capellans could bring to bear.

Captured Vulpes BattleMechs became prized trophies for both Draconis Combine samurai and Capellan Confederation janshi, with examples observed on New Syrtis and Robinson operating under enemy colors. At least one disaffected AFFS company commander took his Vulpes when he deserted to form an independent mercenary company, further spreading the design beyond Davion space. This proliferation, while unwelcome to AFFS High Command, served as evidence of the design's combat effectiveness and the high regard in which it was held by MechWarriors across the Inner Sphere.

By 3151, the political sphere had shifted dramatically. The Achernar BattleMechs facility on New Avalon fell under Draconis Combine control during the upheavals of the ilClan era, bringing Vulpes production under new management. Whether the Combine will continue producing the design or redirect the factory's output remains to be seen, but the Vulpes' proven combat record makes it a valuable addition to any faction's arsenal.

text.notes: Notes: Features the following Design Quirks: Stable, Protected Actuators, Non-Standard Parts.
Features the following Design Quirks: Searchlight, Stable.

text.deployment: This custom variant of the 6K replaced the SRM launcher and its ammunition with four tons of advanced communications equipment, transforming the Warhammer into a dedicated command-and-control platform. While retaining the arm-mounted PPCs and torso-mounted medium lasers as its primary armament, the conversion sacrificed all close-range missile capability to dramatically enhance the pilot's ability to coordinate battalion-level operations. The additional communications gear extended the 'Mech's effective command range significantly beyond standard models, making it well suited for directing combined-arms formations from behind the main battle line.

A Star League-era variant produced exclusively for the Draconis Combine, the 6Rk was introduced around 2745 and represented a radical departure from standard Warhammer doctrine. An extralight fusion engine replaced the standard VOX 280 power plant, boosting top speed to eighty-six kilometers per hour and enabling the seventy-ton 'Mech to keep pace with many medium-weight designs. The weight savings were reinvested in thirteen tons of armor, a substantial increase over the original ten, while fifteen double heat sinks managed the thermal output from the unchanged weapon suite. This combination of speed, protection, and firepower made the 6Rk one of the most formidable Warhammer variants of the Star League era, though the complexity of its XL engine limited production to Amalgamated Sword and Steel's advanced manufacturing facilities on Oldsmith.

Alternate Configuration A trades the overwhelming PPC firepower of the Primary for a more versatile generalist loadout. A pair of ER Large Lasers provides long-range striking power, supported by an LB 10-X Autocannon capable of firing both solid and cluster rounds and an LRM-15 for missile fire support. A Streak SRM-6 launcher adds close-range punch with guaranteed hit efficiency. This combination of weapons allows the Warhawk A to engage effectively at multiple range brackets, making it well-suited for fluid engagements where a commander cannot predict the engagement distance.

Alternate Configuration C stands as a deliberate attempt to address the chronic heat management challenges inherent in PPC-heavy Warhawk loadouts. By replacing two of the Primary's four ER PPCs with a pair of Large Pulse Lasers, the configuration reduces peak heat generation while maintaining formidable direct-fire capability. The combination of two ER PPCs and two Large Pulse Lasers, all enhanced by the Targeting Computer, creates a devastating volley at medium to long range. A Flamer provides anti-infantry capability, and three additional double heat sinks further improve thermal management, though even this is not always sufficient during sustained engagements.

Introduced in the years following the Battle of Tukayyid, Alternate Configuration D incorporates newer Clan weapon systems developed during the post-Invasion technological renaissance. A pair of ER Large Lasers serves as the primary energy armament, complemented by an Ultra Autocannon/10 capable of double-rate fire. The configuration's most notable addition is an ATM-9 launcher, which provides unprecedented tactical flexibility through its ability to fire ammunition optimized for long, medium, or short range engagements with correspondingly increasing warhead yields. An ER Small Laser rounds out the armament for point defense.

Alternate Configuration E was introduced by the Fire Mandrills and is a surprising departure from established Warhawk doctrine. Mounting an ER PPC and a Large Pulse Laser alongside three Plasma Cannons, the configuration brings significant thermal warfare capability to the battlefield. The triple plasma cannons can overwhelm enemy heat management systems while the energy weapons deliver precise direct damage. This loadout reflects the Fire Mandrills' willingness to experiment with unconventional weapon combinations, producing a configuration that excels at degrading enemy combat effectiveness through heat saturation rather than raw damage output alone.

Alternate Configuration G abandons the Warhawk's traditional long-range philosophy entirely, transforming it into a devastating short-range juggernaut. A massive LB 20-X Autocannon dominates the right arm, capable of delivering either concentrated slugs or devastating cluster rounds at close range. The left arm mounts paired Improved Heavy Large Lasers and a Streak SRM-6, providing additional close-quarters firepower. A Supercharger allows the normally ponderous assault 'Mech to rapidly close to optimum engagement distance, where the Targeting Computer ensures maximum efficiency from every salvo. This configuration is designed to end engagements quickly and violently once it reaches its preferred range bracket.

Alternate Configuration H was introduced by Clan Star Adder to showcase their heavy laser technology. The configuration mounts paired Large Pulse Lasers and paired Heavy Large Lasers, creating an immensely powerful close-to-medium range energy weapons battery. An LRM-10 provides the only concession to long-range combat. Four additional double heat sinks attempt to manage the tremendous thermal output of the heavy laser array, though sustained fire remains a challenge. The H configuration epitomizes the close-range brawler approach, relying on the Warhawk's substantial armor and the sheer destructive power of its energy weapons to overwhelm opponents before heat becomes critical.

Alternate Configuration I is built as a dedicated long-range sniper, carrying an ER PPC and an ER Large Laser in each arm for a devastating four-weapon direct-fire battery at extended ranges. An LRM-5 and SRM-6 in the center torso provide supplementary firepower, while additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load of sustained energy fire. With the standard Targeting Computer enhancing every direct-fire weapon, the I configuration can deliver punishing accurate fire at ranges where most opponents struggle to respond effectively, making it one of the most feared long-range configurations in the Warhawk's arsenal.

The Primary configuration embodies the Warhawk's role as a devastating long-range assault platform. Armed with four ER PPCs linked to the standard Targeting Computer, it delivers one of the most accurate and punishing energy barrages of any OmniMech in service. An LRM-10 provides supplementary long-range fire, though the configuration's true strength lies in its ability to employ volley fire tactics with the ER PPCs, alternating weapon groups to maintain a steady stream of accurate firepower while managing the substantial heat generated. This loadout made the Warhawk the terror of the Clan Invasion corridors and established the design's fearsome reputation among Inner Sphere forces.

Alternate Configuration T is a mixed-technology brawler configuration representing the Scorpion Empire's pragmatic approach to resource utilization. The right arm carries twin Inner Sphere-grade Plasma Rifles with three tons of ammunition, while the left arm mounts paired Clan-tech ER PPCs for long-range precision fire. A Rocket Launcher 10 in the center torso provides a one-shot burst of additional firepower. This blending of Inner Sphere and Clan technology reflects the Scorpion Empire's access to Hanseatic League manufacturing infrastructure and their willingness to integrate proven Inner Sphere weapons systems alongside traditional Clan equipment when tactically advantageous.

text.deployment: Fielded during the Draconis Combine's early thirty-second century invasion of the Draconis March, this variant is a field-expedient refit designed to counter the advanced armor composites employed by Combine forces. The entire original weapons suite is stripped and replaced with a large re-engineered laser as the primary weapon, supported by a pair of ER flamers mounted on the same arm. A pair of Magshots on the opposite arm provide supplementary firepower and anti-infantry capability. The re-engineered laser's ability to bypass reflective and hardened armor coatings makes this variant particularly effective against the specialty plating that had rendered older Watchman armaments less effective. Though born of desperation, the focused anti-armor mission profile suited the defensive fighting that characterized the Draconis March campaigns of this period.

Debuting in 3144 at the New Hartford Gardens arena on Solaris VII, this custom variant is an experiment in bringing master-and-drone technology to BattleMech dueling. Backed by the Duchy of Andurien, the design features a modified command console that allows a copilot to control a heavyweight drone, a modified Vulpes refit. The armament is completely reworked around a large re-engineered laser supported by four ER medium lasers, a combination that taxes the twelve double heat sinks but provides substantial striking power against opponents in the same weight class. A 200-rated light engine saves mass at the cost of survivability, while seven tons of ferro-fibrous armor provides adequate protection. The real advantage lies in the Clan-spec Watchdog composite electronic warfare system, which combines active probe and ECM capabilities to disrupt adversary sensors while maintaining reliable control links to the accompanying drone even through hostile electronic interference.

text.overview:
The Whitworth was first manufactured in 2610 as a medium BattleMech intended to fill the weight gap between the lighter Wasp and heavier Phoenix Hawk designs. Originally conceived as a missile support platform for scout and strike lances, the Whitworth emerged from the Whitworth Company's design bureau on Dieron as a competent if unremarkable machine. Known colloquially as the "Tin Woodsman" among both critics and admirers, the design offered respectable firepower and adequate armor protection for its intended fire support role.

Despite an enduring reputation for mechanical unreliability in its lower actuator systems, the Whitworth proved serviceable enough to see widespread deployment across the Star League and its successor states, earning a place as a rugged if ungainly workhorse in armies throughout the Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The Whitworth's primary armament consists of two Longbow-10 LRM launchers mounted in the torsos, providing substantial long-range firepower for a medium 'Mech. These weapons are slaved to the Garret D2J targeting system (the same anti-aircraft tracking system employed by the Rifleman and Quickdraw) giving respectable accuracy against aerial and ground targets alike. Three Intek medium lasers provide adequate close-range defense when enemies close the distance.

The design's most significant limitation is its slow maximum speed of 64 km/h, over 30 km/h slower than the Wasps and Phoenix Hawks it was designed to support. Four Whitworth Jetlift jump jets split between the legs partially compensate for this deficiency. Eight tons of Durallex Light armor provide reasonable protection, distributed heavily around the legs to protect the design's notorious weak point, a faulty actuator system in the hips and legs that can cause limbs to tear loose during aggressive maneuvering. Houses have been known to replace failed legs with those salvaged from other 'Mech designs, creating bizarre but functional hybrids.
text.deployment: A Draconis Combine variant introduced in 3070 by Whitworth Specialty Manufacturing, this variant utilizes two MML-7 launchers that allow the pilot to switch between long-range missile support and close-quarters SRM fire as tactical situations demand. Five QuestStar improved jump jets enable jumps of up to 150 meters, providing excellent mobility particularly suited to urban combat environments. A C3 slave unit allows the design to share targeting telemetry with lance mates, making it an effective fire support node in combined-arms formations.
text.battleHistory:
The Whitworth's origins trace to the Reunification War era, when the Whitworth Company on Dieron sought to create a medium fire support platform for Star League forces. The original WTH-1S model carried Harpoon-6 SRM launchers that encouraged pilots to engage in close-range combat for which the design was poorly suited, resulting in heavy losses. By 2689, Star League defense planners mandated the replacement of these weapons with Longbow-10 LRM launchers, creating the WTH-1 that would become the standard production model.

During the Star League era, the Whitworth served in both SLDF scout units and mobile strike lances, often deployed alongside Wolverines and Phoenix Hawks for reconnaissance-in-force missions, or providing fire support to heavier formations of Riflemen and Warhammers. The Rim Worlds Republic also fielded Whitworths, including the infamous WTH-0 variant used to devastating effect during the Amaris Civil War, where Republic forces employed inferno missiles and flamers to raze entire cities.

The destruction of the Whitworth Company's Dieron facility in 2776 during the Amaris Crisis eliminated the primary source of spare parts, condemning surviving Whitworths to gradual attrition throughout the Succession Wars. By the end of this era, fewer than three hundred remained operational, mostly in the hands of MechWarrior families who had passed the machines down through generations. The design earned the unflattering nickname "Worthless" among Federated Suns and Draconis Combine pilots, though the 'Mechs themselves continued to serve their units well.

The situation changed in 3035 when Whitworth Specialty Manufacturing was incorporated on Benjamin, reportedly with ComStar assistance as part of aid offered to Theodore Kurita. This company began producing spare parts and later developed upgrade kits following the Clan Invasion. Despite these efforts, most Whitworths were decommissioned from Great House militaries by the mid-3050s, finding new homes among mercenary companies and Periphery nations like the Taurian Concordat and Outworlds Alliance.

The Jihad prompted renewed interest in the platform, with both the Federated Suns and Draconis Combine developing C3-equipped variants to counter Blakist improved C3 technology. More recently, Marian Arms Inc. on Alphard has begun producing an improved variant that has spread throughout the Inner Sphere via salvage and Draconis Combine contracts, ensuring the Whitworth's continued presence on battlefields across known space.
